# STAR ancestor matching: direction-gated source audit

Read-only audit of runtime52f32dd. No core changes, project runs, JVMs or new tests. Read the complete policy as **summary matching**, not a change to instruction edge transfer. The user example concerns actual`p.*/FLOW`; whether concrete`p.*/T` is included is a separate behavior decision.

## 1. A precise candidate policy

Keep these concepts separate:

```text
input annotation: actual.tail == STAR       // not premise.tail == STAR
position: actual leaf is a STRICT ancestor of the summary premise
source role: CURRENT / SAVED_DIRECT / SAVED_OPPOSITE
```

`SAVED_OPPOSITE` means storedRecord.direction != currentRun.direction. It is not simply BACKWARD. A backward current publication is DIRECT; a saved backward record read in a forward run is OPPOSITE. Current reversed instruction forms are not saved opposite-direction summaries.

The narrow candidate directly addressing the example is:

```text
allowStarAncestor(actual, role) =
    actual is not FlowTree || actual.tail != STAR || role == SAVED_OPPOSITE
```

An all-STAR candidate would remove the FlowTree guard and must separately cover concrete STAR/T inputs. It is a larger change.

Preserve the existing at-node, below-node, mark, E/mx and protection rules. In`Summary.insidePart`, gate only the STAR contribution of strict ancestor spine nodes while walking the premise path. Do not set the entire`inside` flag false: insidePart also contains equal-path cells that do not represent the disputed ancestor case. The low-level `record=true` flag separately enables applicable/below matching, so it cannot stand in for this direction permission.

MAY and MUST ancestor matching remain unchanged. The established MUST and cut-to-MAY finding controls would fail under a blanket inside removal. A STAR **premise** can receive MAY or MUST actuals, and an EXACT premise can receive an ancestor STAR actual; filtering by premise tail therefore implements the wrong policy.

## 2. Complete matching-path inventory

The final native predicate is`ApOps.satisfying` →`Summary.satisfyingPart`. Candidates can remain broad; changing a final predicate does not require changing native candidate ordering.

| Path | Existing entry point | Required role for this candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Physical current summary replay/publication | `SubscriptionManager.matches:10–15`; same matcher serves replay and delivery | CURRENT, in either run direction |
| Physical saved same-direction summary | `PersistedSummaryReplay:22–30`, record.direction == direction, record=true | SAVED_DIRECT |
| Physical saved opposite-direction view | `PersistedSummaryReplay:32–43`, forEachReversedAt +record=true | SAVED_OPPOSITE |
| Current local block DATA | `BlockSummaryLinks.queueData:152–165`; matched envelope reused atdeliver:208 | CURRENT; gate before match-once envelope, not after application |
| Local saved direct | `MethodBlockRuntime.replaySaved:428–443` →`LocalRelationApplication.matchRecord:66–71` | SAVED_DIRECT; preserve one native match/MUST lane split across all output scalars |
| Local saved reverse | `MethodBlockRuntime.applySavedView:463–478` →`LocalRelationApplication.applyRecordView:88–99` | SAVED_OPPOSITE; retain exact inverse-view protection andports |
| Pure loop consumer saved direct | `LoopConsumerObservation:96–100` →application.applyRecord | SAVED_DIRECT, exactly matching actual replay |
| Pure loop consumer saved reverse | `LoopConsumerObservation:101–104` →application.applyRecordView | SAVED_OPPOSITE, exactly matching actual replay |
| Current ND AP row | physical matching selects each member; localqueueData caches a matched member before the complete NdSummaryJoin | CURRENT for each arm; keep complete joins/origins/layers, never split executable ND |
| Saved native AP ND | none | Record.premise is InitialAp; native records are normal singleton summaries. ND rawTarget rows are separate. |
| Current Target and saved NormalTarget | `RunMethodCallServices.applyTarget:494–505`; local`targetArmLayer:132–143` | CURRENT or SAVED_DIRECT. `saved=true` does not mean opposite; NormalTarget is ignored backward. Do not accidentally grant opposite permission to all saved Targets. |
| Pure saved Target arm | `LoopConsumerObservation:108–117` | Same native Target matcher; its metadata arm is not an executable completed NDjoin. |
| Run-1 live static summary binding | `RunMethodCallServices.applyStaticInput:453–480`, `BlockRunState:433–454` | CURRENT/direct static lane, not opposite |
| Joined static writer/input binding | `OwnedJoinedStaticWriterBinding:91–96` | DIRECT retained source, no saved-record reversal |
| Reserved static continuation request relay | `StaticBoundaryInputRequests:45` | Direct identity/request lane; not an opposite native record |

The source role belongs to the matching invocation, not Facts/InitialAp equality or one mutable ApMode flag. The same method and AP manager serve mixed direct/reverse operations. Saved matching still keeps its own record-mode geometry and the special native MUST definite/provisional lane logic.

CallServices.applyRecord/applyRecordView and local applyMatched consume an already selected input. They must not rematch under a different role. Physical/local current queues and the pure observer must agree; otherwise actual delivery and prefix-trial signatures diverge. Target behavior and static metadata protocols should be explicitly in scope or explicitly retained, rather than silently reclassified as opposite.

Do not change:

- C2 initial emission/canStoreInitial and C5 pair budgets by accident;
- statement/call-binding micro-edge application, `EdgeApplication` ancestor transfers, fieldreads/writes and source/cleaner rules;
- MAY/MUST matching, original premise union, protection and marked demand;
- saved port reversal or canonical common loop-exit ownership;
- SourceHit/Target generation and original actual-input identity.

## 3. What source grammar proves about forward/current replacement

### Run-1

`Run1RequestMatching.validateRun1Initial:78–101` requires every nonstatic initial to have an empty concrete path. A current nonstatic summary therefore cannot have a deeper field premise than an ancestor STAR input in run-1. This includes method-owned blocks: they use the same run-1 abstraction/validation. A proposed counterexample with a current run-1`p.f.*` summary is illegal under the actual initial grammar.

Static FLOW initials are named class+field anchors; class-only concrete markers are EXACT. The ordinary static field and continuation identities use canonical named anchors, so these are not an automatic class-wide STAR-inside exception. Nevertheless keep their native matching role explicit, not inferred from a fake reversed-record tag.

### Restricted runs3+

`DemandStore.validateRestricted:98–110` asserts FLOW demand entries are ANY; STAR entries are permitted only in run-2. HandOff/BlockHandOff separately assert restricted FLOW demand conclusions are ANY, and guidancePattern maps MUST toANY.

For an actual FLOW STAR packet, C2 against ANY emits only from a strict descendant actual path. The emitted first-new-field prefix is at or above that actual path. Same-prefix or ancestor STAR actuals do not answer an ANY entry. Consequently, a current callee admitted from such an actual already receives an initial whose path is no deeper than the actual. It can analyze that input without needing a deeper current summary originating at a different input initial.

This is a useful replacement invariant for **current** matches. It is not a whole-engine completion theorem: it needs transfer monotonicity in the selected normal suffix-relation semantics, identical rule/protection effects and complete worklist analysis of the admitted initial. In run-1 that proper-ancestor current case is absent; run-2's allowed STAR demand is an explicit exception needing separate proof/control.

### Saved direct has no such guarantee

Persisted replay runs before C2, even when current demand is empty. RecordStore retains each normal singleton in its producing direction; it does not guarantee an opposite-direction counterpart for each saved direct record. A backward run may never enter that method or may produce only DEMAND rows. The fact that opposite matching remains enabled therefore does not itself prove a replacement exists.

Example shape, not an asserted new end-to-end false negative:

```java
Object read(Box p) { return p.f; }
// A later forward analysis can infer normal p.f.*/FLOW -> ret.*/FLOW.
// Its root p.*/FLOW -> ret.[any]/FLOW alternative need not be NORMAL/persisted.
```

A saved direct field reader has no required shorter identity reader: `p.*→ret.*` would be a different Java transfer. On a root STAR/FLOW actual it currently provides a provisional MAY result. Disabling that one abstract result could still be complete through concrete mark packets, but no source contract proves such a concrete shadow exists for every AP query and effect.

Thus “current input is reanalyzed” cannot justify blanket saved-direct removal. A concrete-shadow/permission invariant is the missing global theorem, not something record.direction implies.

## 4. The S/L pair: useful invariant and remaining reverse mismatch

For emptyE/mx normal suffix copies in one exact interface:

```text
S: p.a.*   -> q.b.*
L: p.a.r.* -> q.b.r.*
```

Every concrete correlated pair of L is in S: choose the same appendedr+suffix on both sides. This is stronger than output prefix coverage. Also:

```text
FL(L.out)-FL(L.in) == FL(S.out)-FL(S.in)
```

because the same suffix is counted on both sides. Reversal preserves the equality. The fixed-premise MUST growth-classifier counterexample from yesterday does not apply to this same-suffix STAR pair.

At a concrete at/below input, S/L native transfer agrees. The earlier native control proves`p.f.g.$/T` produces`q.f.g.$/T` under both. The new narrow DIRECT policy intentionally removes the extra ancestor-STAR widening result; old native results were:

```text
actual p.*/FLOW NORMAL
S => q.*/FLOW NORMAL
L => q.f.[any]/FLOW DEMAND
```

But after deleting L from a forward NORMAL record inventory, opposite matching alone does not preserve every former backward observation:

```text
backward views:
S^-1: q.*   -> p.*
L^-1: q.f.* -> p.f.*
actual q.*/FLOW NORMAL
S^-1 => p.*/FLOW NORMAL
L^-1 => p.f.[any]/FLOW DEMAND   // still permitted by new OPPOSITE inside
```

That abstract progress label disappears if L no longer exists. This is a source-derived symmetric instance of the already native-checked forward application geometry, not a new native run. Proving same real flows/findings may be possible, but exact native observation-set equivalence is already false. The grouped C2 controls also show that spatial coverage cannot automatically replace every lost refinement label.

## 5. Concrete STAR scope is an additional gap

If the proposal covers all actual STAR facts, rather than FLOW only, C2 and direct application can disagree even on a legal pair of shapes:

```text
Dc = p.f.*/T
actual = p.*/T DEMAND
C2 => initial p.f.$/T DEMAND
old direct matcher => inside=true
new all-STAR strict-ancestor direct matcher => false
```

This follows `RestrictedInitialPolicy:53–56`. Concrete STAR demands are allowed in restricted handoff; they are not subject to the FLOW-ANY assertion. Concrete STAR/T actuals are the normal provisional request/first-field refinement form. A callee admitted under the deeper exact initial could publish a result that the same original offer can no longer consume. No normal opposite record is required by these APIs. This is a valid source-level C2/application compatibility hole; a full code/iteration witness has not been constructed here. The narrow FlowTree-only version avoids this extra change.

## 6. Conclusion and proof boundary

There is a coherent narrow candidate: disable only strict ancestor **FLOW STAR** contributions for DIRECT current/saved matching, preserve opposite native views, and preserve all ordinary instruction/MAY/MUST/at-node behavior. It aligns the disputed direct S/L application on STAR/FLOW with correlated relation coverage.

However, existing source proves only limited current-run grammar/reanalysis facts. It does not prove universal saved-direct replacement by opposite records or concrete shadow packets, and S/L removal still changes some opposite-direction abstract progress labels. This is a selected abstract-summary policy change, not merely an implementation speedup under exact old native observations. Before implementation, close the FULL concrete/source-permission completeness theorem and run-2 exception, and decide explicit scope for concrete STAR, Targets and predefined reversed models. No need to generalize or redesign ordinary field transfers to test this proposal.

proofBoundary: Run1 grammar and late current-C2 shape invariants are source facts. Universal FULL concrete-shadow completeness, saved-direct replacement and run2 exception are not proved. The reverse extra-label example is source-derived from existing native geometry, not new execution.

conservativeCandidatePolicy.subject: Final summary matching only; ordinary instruction edges, call bindings, cleaners, sources and field transfers are unchanged.

roleDefinition.CURRENT: Current-run publication in the run direction, even when that direction is BACKWARD.
roleDefinition.SAVED_DIRECT: Stored native Record.direction equals current run.direction.
roleDefinition.SAVED_OPPOSITE: Stored native Record.direction differs from current run.direction; use the genuine transient reversed read view.

conservativeCandidatePolicy.narrowFormula: allowStarAncestor = !(actual is FlowTree && actual.tail == STAR) || role == SAVED_OPPOSITE
conservativeCandidatePolicy.allStarAlternative: allowStarAncestor = actualTail != STAR || role == SAVED_OPPOSITE; wider change includes concrete STAR/T request and refinement facts and requires separate completeness proof.
conservativeCandidatePolicy.geometry: Only strict ancestor spine contributions from STAR actuals are gated. Existing at-node and below matching stays; insidePart cannot be disabled wholesale.
conservativeCandidatePolicy.annotations: Preserve actual layers, full marks, both exclusions, taint protection, whole original premise, native record matching flags/MUST lane split and exact owner ports.
conservativeCandidatePolicy.metadata: Role is invocation metadata. Do not add role to Facts/InitialAp/RecordLeafView semantic equality, use a global mutable ApMode switch or classify every BACKWARD current row as opposite.
conservativeCandidatePolicy.targetsAndPredefined: Scope undecided: saved NormalTarget is forward/direct, not a reverse Record; predefined models syntactically reversed by interpreter need an explicit decision. No Target/ND rule behavior is silently changed.

physicalOrder: replayPersistedSummaries on every complete original offer
replay applicable saved nonzero NormalTarget rows forward
skip only current subscription/analysis if C2 is empty
localOrder: skip current child-state analysis when initials empty
savedReplayBeforeC2.consequence: Deleting a demand row does NOT stop saved records from being queried on an already offered packet. No such claim is made. A separate proof would be needed if a different upstream change prevents the packet from being offered at all.
savedReplayBeforeC2.remainingGap: The grammar/current reanalysis argument does not guarantee an opposite counterpart or concrete shadow for every saved DIRECT STAR/FLOW match when current demand is empty.

scopeQuestions: Is the user-selected STAR actual policy limited to FlowTree STAR, or does it include concrete TaintTree STAR/T?
Does inside mean strict ancestor only (the motivating case), retaining equal-path cells?
Does opposite mean stored producer direction differs from current run direction, rather than syntactic reversal or all BACKWARD execution?
Should typed Target matching remain unchanged, or use the same direct/opposite distinction? Saved NormalTargets have no opposite backward replay.
How should predefined model reversals be classified?
What completeness invariant justifies saved-direct replacement and run-2 exception beyond the source-proved late current-C2 prefix property?
summaryOfEstablishedFacts: Run1 current nonstatic initial paths are empty, so motivating strict-ancestor versus deeper current summary initial is absent.
Restricted runs3+ FLOW entry demands are ANY, so a current callee admitted from FLOW STAR gets a first-new-field initial no deeper than the actual leaf.
Saved direct replay occurs beforeC2 and doesnot require current demand.
Same-suffix STAR S/L preserve FL(out)-FL(in), including reversal; the earlier fixed-premise MUST classifier split is not the same case.
Deleting L still changes some old opposite-direction STAR/FLOW→ANY/DEMAND labels, so exact old native observation-set equivalence is not proved.
All-STAR scope has a legal scalar C2/application mismatch on concrete STAR/T; production full-run reachability/FN is unproved here.
